transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-20
Start time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~36 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Brooks (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Orion PM), Luca Romano (Orion ML Eng), Priya Nair (Orion CTO)

Summary (auto): quick discovery for PLG quickstart. Orion wants to spin up hosted API trial, evaluate latency and cost, and understand path to Dedicated/Private for regulated workloads.

00:00 Samira: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Samira from Redwood, AE for your account, and with me is Ethan our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
00:06 Maya: Hey, yeah good, thanks. Maya here. Excited to learn more, we onboarded through the quickstart link.
00:10 Priya: Priya here. Only joining for the first 15. Want to make sure security + path to private is clear.
00:15 Ethan: Great, I'll cover the quickstart flow and some performance notes; Samira will talk credits and next steps.
00:21 Samira: Quick agenda — time-to-first-token, what free credits include, hosted vs dedicated/private tradeoffs, security questions, and next steps. Sound good?
00:26 Maya: Yes. We're a PLG org, want to get devs integrated this week if possible. Questions around rate limits, cost, and data retention.
00:34 Luca: Also curious about latency for our smaller models — we have chat endpoints that need sub-200ms p50 ideally.
00:40 Ethan: Helpful — are those 200ms on simple prompts or long-context?
00:44 Luca: Mostly short prompts, 64-128 tokens, sometimes with a small KV cache per user.
00:49 Ethan: OK that maps well to hosted; our quickstart usually gets you to first token in under 15 minutes. The free credits org we can enable will let you run a few hundred calls and do a smoke test for latency and cost.
00:58 Maya: Can you remind me what the quickstart includes? We clicked sign up but didn't get the credits step.
01:02 Samira: Yes — we provide a trial org and $500 in free credits for new accounts by default for PLG signups, plus quickstart docs and SDK examples. I'll enable an account for your team and share the onboarding link.
01:12 Priya: Is that $500 sufficient for a realistic smoke test? We have a 1M request/day projection at scale but initial dev is smaller.
01:19 Samira: It's generally enough for initial dev and a few benchmarks. For larger pilots we move to a short reserved capacity or a POC where we provide a dedicated bench environment. We can talk through pilot sizing after you share traffic profile.
01:29 Luca: When you say hosted, what happens to KV cache and user data? Is that stored in Redwood infra? We need to be careful about PII.
01:36 Ethan: Good question. By default hosted uses our managed runtime and ephemeral KV cache — not persisted outside request unless you call persistence features. For regulated data we recommend either Dedicated with customer VPC peering or Private deployment where you control the network and KMS/HSM.
01:48 Maya: Do you have SOC 2 and ISO certs?
01:51 Ethan: We're SOC 2 Type II. We also provide audit logs, RBAC, SSO via SAML/OIDC, and KMS integrations for Dedicated/Private. I'll drop the security pack — the security whitepaper and SOC 2 report — into the folder.
02:02 Priya: For Private, how long is the lead time and what's required network-wise? We have air-gapped segments for some projects.
02:07 Samira: Private can be packaged for on-prem or VPC-based installs. Lead time depends on scope — a standard VPC private control plane typically takes 4–6 weeks with engineering engagement; air-gapped on-prem is longer and requires more ops lift. For many customers we start on hosted, then migrate to Dedicated, and if needed move to Private.
02:23 Priya: That path makes sense. We want a predictable migration story.
02:27 Maya: Back to quickstart — whats the SDK? Do we have node/python examples?
02:31 Ethan: Yes, we have first-party SDKs for Node and Python and examples for chat, streaming, embeddings, and function calling. The quickstart repo includes a Hello World that gets a first token in under a minute. There might be occasional minor transcription issues in docs but the examples work.
02:44 Luca: On latency — you said hosted can meet sub-200ms p50 for small prompts, but we've seen big variance with other vendors. How do you handle batching and SLOs?
02:53 Ethan: Our runtime does continuous batching and smart routing. For low-latency sync requests we route to low-queue workers and can pin model variants to reduce jitter. Batching is workload-aware so it won't add large tail latencies for small prompt distributions. For strict SLOs we recommend Dedicated with reserved GPU pools.
03:08 Maya: Cost — what's the ballpark for hosted vs dedicated? We care about price per token and also about predictable unit economics.
03:14 Samira: Hosted is usage-based and good for dev and early PLG. Dedicated is reserved capacity — better at scale and gives predictable throughput and lower per-token cost if your volume justifies it. We can share a cost model spreadsheet. I'll attach a sample that maps requests/seq-length to expected monthly spend.
03:27 Luca: Any limits on concurrency? Our throughput could spike with viral usage.
03:31 Ethan: For hosted we have soft rate limits that can be increased. For spikes, smart routing and burst capacity can help, but for sustained high throughput we recommend Dedicated.
03:40 Maya: Can we get a test org with the SDK and run a basic microservice in our staging this week?
03:44 Samira: Yes. I'll create a trial org, enable the $500 credits, and invite your team. Expect an email with the quickstart link and docs by tomorrow.
03:52 Priya: Perfect. Also need to see audit log samples and SAML setup doc.
03:56 Ethan: I'll share the security pack and the SAML SSO guide. Also I can prep a technical deep-dive that runs a 1K-sample latency benchmark against your prompt set — wants me to do that?
04:06 Priya: Yes please. That will be helpful to validate the POC.
04:09 Luca: I'll put together ~50-100 representative prompts and a traffic profile and drop them in the shared folder by Friday.
04:15 Samira: Great. Recap — Samira: enable trial + credits; Samira to share pricing and cost spreadsheet; Ethan to share security docs and schedule benchmark deep-dive; Luca/Maya to provide prompt set and traffic profiles. Anyone else?
04:27 Maya: No that's it. Also can you call out any gotchas on model selection? We may start with smaller open models and move to proprietary later.
04:34 Ethan: For model selection, smaller quantized open models are cheaper but watch for quality regressions on long contexts. Redwood offers model profiles and quantization recommendations in the console; for production we test on your eval prompts to verify. We also support automatic fallback to higher-capacity variants if latency and quality tradeoffs warrant.
04:50 Priya: OK good. How do we handle secrets and KMS in Dedicated?
04:54 Ethan: In Dedicated/Private you can bring your own KMS or connect to a hosted KMS via customer-managed keys; secrets are encrypted at rest and in transit, and audit logs are available for every request.
05:03 Samira: Any remaining blockers on your side for getting started?
05:07 Maya: No blockers, main ask is quick access and the security docs.
05:11 Priya: I'll only rejoin the deep-dive but otherwise good.
05:15 Samira: Thanks everyone — I'll send the invite and next steps, and we'll aim to have the trial enabled by tomorrow.
05:20 Luca: Thanks.
05:22 Meeting end.
